key_insight: No single intra-patient 3D multimodal registration method is robust across anatomies and modalities, and geometric overlap metrics can disagree strongly with image-based correspondence metrics.
engineering_relevance: For clinical image-registration pipelines, model choice should be benchmarked with multiple complementary metrics, not just Dice or Hausdorff distance, to avoid misleading deployment decisions.
method: Benchmarked classical optimization-based and modern learning-based deformable registration methods, including deep learning and foundation models.
Tested on three datasets spanning different anatomy and difficulty levels, covering synthetic deformation recovery and real clinical scenarios.
Evaluated with DSC, HD95, and MIND-SSC to compare geometric alignment and modality-independent structural similarity.
evidence_signal: The benchmark shows high performance variability by dataset: learning-based methods are strongest on large synthetic benchmarks, while gains are limited in real pelvic registration and metric disagreement is common.
watch_item: Anatomy-guided approaches may optimize segmented-region overlap while degrading global alignment outside labels, so deployment should verify full-volume deformation quality.
paper_title: Benchmarking Intra-Patient 3D Deformable Multimodal Image Registration
